title: まるで — just like ～, as if ～
summary: An adverb for likening something to another thing that it is not. It appears as まるで～のようだ, まるで～みたいだ, or まるで～かのようだ.

patterns.form: まるで＋N／V普通形＋ようだ（みたいだ）
patterns.gloss: まるで + noun / plain form + ようだ

patterns.form: まるで＋V普通形＋かのように
patterns.gloss: まるで + plain form + かのように

body.p: 彼女の手はまるで氷のように冷たい compares her hands to ice to stress how cold they are, though they are not real ice. It is used together with ようだ.

body.h: かのように vs ようだ
body.p: まるで～かのように says someone acts as if something were true when it is not: 店員はまるで何も知らないかのように話した. To compare directly to a noun, use ～のよう (絵のようだ).

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）の手（て）はまるで氷（こおり）のように冷（つめ）たい。
examples.romaji: Kanojo no te wa marude kōri no yō ni tsumetai.
examples.tr: Her hands are cold, just like ice.

examples.ja: その村（むら）の景色（けしき）は、まるで絵（え）のようだった。
examples.romaji: Sono mura no keshiki wa, marude e no yō datta.
examples.tr: The scenery of that village was just like a painting.

examples.ja: 店員（てんいん）はまるで何（なに）も知（し）らないかのように話（はな）した。
examples.romaji: Ten'in wa marude nani mo shiranai ka no yō ni hanashita.
examples.tr: The clerk spoke as if he knew nothing at all.

pitfalls: After まるで use ようだ or みたいだ; do not end with a flat statement.
まるで～ない also exists in a different sense meaning 'not at all.'
